title: Template overview reports tenant overrides per template
detail: template-resolver has a SystemAdmin query tenant-override-counts, and the overview rows for system templates carry overriddenBy { active, total } for SystemAdmins. The designer's overview reads it instead of issuing one tenant-overrides query per row. Reading it uses a declared unsafeRaw escape hatch because it counts across tenants.

title: Titles for the template-resolver write handlers
detail: Every agent-callable template-resolver write handler now has a title in de, en, es, fr and it, so the AI assistant names actions such as "Edit template draft" instead of "template-resolver:write:patch-draft". The handlers of mounted content collections (`<id>-set`) stay untitled because their names depend on the app. The empty-field hint of the placeholder line editor now ends in an ellipsis inside the field instead of running past it.

title: Overrides of locked templates are no longer served
detail: A tenant override of a mail, PDF or layout template is delivered (mail send, PDF render, linked PDFs, layouts, previews, export bundles, document blocks, overview, text blocks) only while the template is listed in tenantEditable. A locked override stays stored and has no effect; listing the template makes it effective again, nothing is deleted. A SystemAdmin sees locked overrides in the overview (`lockedOverride`, `lockedOverrideI18nKey`) and can reset or archive them with the existing handlers; the template-resolver queries do not show them to a TenantAdmin; the audit log keeps the history. Tenant rows of a collection mounted with `access` are served, except for a slug that has a system template outside tenantEditable: that system template wins, and the collection `-set` handler refuses such a slug for a non-SystemAdmin. createTemplateResolverApi(db) became createTemplateResolverApi(db, registry) because the delivery policy is read from the mounted feature; without the mounted feature no tenant override is served.
migration: Overrides of templates that are not tenantEditable are no longer served; enable the template via tenantEditable to keep using them. Pass the registry as second argument to createTemplateResolverApi (ctx.registry in handlers, stack.registry in tests). Tenant rows without a system counterpart (for example text blocks seeded directly into a tenant) are hidden as well unless listed in tenantEditable.

title: Overview label for locked template overrides
detail: Adds templateResolver.overview.lockedOverride.

title: Mail rendering follows the template delivery policy
detail: Resolves templates through createTemplateResolverApi(db, registry); overrides of locked templates fall back to the system version.

title: PDF rendering follows the template delivery policy
detail: Resolves templates through createTemplateResolverApi(db, registry); overrides of locked templates fall back to the system version.

title: Samples follow the createTemplateResolverApi(db, registry) signature
detail: Recipes and sample apps build the template resolver API with the registry as second argument.

title: seedSystemTemplate accepts titleI18nKey
detail: A seeded template can store an i18n key as its title (titleI18nKey, exclusive with title). The overview returns the key; the document-designer overview, mail editor and PDF link modal translate it and fall back to the raw text. Templates without a key behave as before; no migration.

title: Document PDFs embed the images of a record
detail: A template variable of type images (templateVariable.images()) holds FileRef ids of the record. The new Images block (div[data-images], PDF templates only, rejected for mail kinds) renders them as data-URI images in the real PDF render. Only files of the rendering tenant are read, only png, jpeg, gif and webp, at most 24 images and 20 MB per document; missing, foreign, oversized or non-image ids are dropped silently. Previews and draft PDFs never read files and show one placeholder box per block. An images variable never renders as inline text. i18n keys template-resolver.documentEditor.images, template-resolver.documentEditor.imagesVariable and templateResolver.errors.document.imagesBlockPdfOnly ship in de, es, fr and it.
migration: Declare a template variable with type `images`, place the Images block, and pass FileRef ids of the record in `variables`. Images resolve only in the real PDF render, previews show placeholders. The ids must come from the record on the server, never from client input: a resolved id is read for the whole tenant without an entity access check.

title: Template editing is SystemAdmin-only unless the app unlocks it
detail: Every tenant write handler, the overview and resource upload accept SystemAdmin only, plus the roles of the tenantEditable entries. A write on a template that is not unlocked fails with templateNotTenantEditable. The test send follows the same rule. For a non-SystemAdmin an unknown template id answers 403 like a locked one, so the response does not reveal whether it exists. Collections without an access rule default to SystemAdmin.
migration: Where TenantAdmins must keep editing a template, pass tenantEditable to createTemplateResolverFeature, for example tenantEditable: [{ kind: "mail", slug: "billing:notify:invoice-issued", access: { roles: ["TenantAdmin"] } }]. Give template collections an explicit access rule if tenants should manage them.

title: send-test-status query for the template test mail
detail: template-resolver:query:send-test-status answers whether a test mail can be sent (canSend) and, if not, why (no_channel or no_address), so clients can disable the action instead of failing on send.

title: seedSystemTemplateBundle sets a title per template
detail: Bundle locale entries accept an optional title, written to the template resource and exported again by the bundle export. SeedSystemTemplateOptions gets title. The template overview shows it instead of the slug.

title: Preview and test mail render with the values of a picked record
detail: `template-resolver:query:preview` and `template-resolver:write:send-test` accept an optional `variables` object that replaces the declared example values for the named variables. The values are checked against the template's variable schema like a real send (unknown names and wrong types are rejected as `variables.<name>` validation errors); variables not passed keep their example. The mail editor now passes the values picked through the preview record picker into the preview and the test mail instead of only listing them.

title: Read a mail or PDF template as blocks and change it with structured operations
detail: The query `template-resolver:query:document-blocks` returns a document template as blocks with stable ids (b0, b1, ...), its meta, variables, allowed block types and uploaded image keys, plus a `base` (scope and version). The write `template-resolver:write:patch-draft` applies up to 50 operations (insertBlock, replaceText, removeBlock, setResource, setMeta, setVariable) to that state and stores the result as the caller's tenant draft; an active version keeps being served until publish. Block ids refer to the state that was read. If the template changed since `base` was read, the call fails with `version_conflict` and writes nothing; a patch that removes a required placeholder or sets variables a notification declares is refused. `writeTemplateRow` accepts an optional `expectedVersion`. The universal helpers `placeholder-text` and the toolbar block sets moved out of `web/` without changing the web exports.

title: Text examples of template variables follow the template's language
detail: The `example` of a text or richText templateVariable is now read like `label`: an i18n key resolves to the translation of the edited template's locale, plain text stays as it is. Preview, the sample values bar and send-test therefore show German examples for a German template. Example values of other types (link, number, enum-like text values) stay as declared; put the explanation of such a value into the variable's label. Apps: register `templateVariable.text({ example: "<app>:mail.example.x" })` and add the key with de, en and es via `r.translations`.

title: templateVariable label accepts an i18n key; the designer shows the translation instead of the raw name
detail: A label given as i18n key (templateVariable.text({ label: "billing:mail.variable.invoiceNumber" }) plus r.translations in each locale) is translated in the designer's variable rail, in the chips on the paper, in the steps and repeat block heads, in the placeholder, button, repeat and steps pickers of the editor toolbar and in the missing-variables footer; the raw variable name stays visible as tooltip. Plain-text labels keep working, a key without translation falls back to the key text. The server preview (sampleValuesFor, now with an optional labelText translator) names sample values by the translated label in the draft's locale. variableLabelMap in document-designer now takes the translator as first argument. VariableChips in the renderer takes optional labels.

title: Notifications can keep their mail template system-only
detail: r.notification(name, { systemOnly: true }) marks the stored mail template as a platform text. Tenant admins no longer see it in the template overview, list or detail, and creating a tenant version (upsert-tenant, copy-locale, import-bundle, also a SystemAdmin writing for a tenant) is refused with access_denied and templateResolver.errors.systemOnlyTemplate. SystemAdmins edit the system template as before, and the mail renderer always uses it, even if a tenant row exists from before.

title: Rich text placeholders no longer nest paragraphs
detail:
A richText placeholder alone in a paragraph compiles into a div that keeps the paragraph attributes, and one inside other text renders inline with line breaks instead of its own paragraphs. Mails and PDFs no longer contain

. richText and stepIs are now reserved template variable names, like the other renderer helpers.
migration: A notification that declares a template variable called richText, stepIs or percent fails at boot; rename the variable.

title: Template bundles with a logo can be seeded
detail: seedSystemTemplateBundle(db, bundle, { dispatcher }) now seeds bundles that carry resources such as a logo by running the import-bundle-system write on the given seed dispatcher. With ifExists "skip" (default) nothing is written when every locale row already exists; if only some exist, the whole bundle is imported again. Without a dispatcher such a bundle still fails with a message that names the missing option.

title: Template conditions with data-if and a percent variable type
detail: A paragraph, heading or table row with data-if="name" renders only when the variable has a value (0 counts as a value); inside a repeat row the name refers to the row field, on the repeat row itself to the root variable. The sanitizer keeps the attribute, and template validation reports a condition on an undeclared variable. New variable type percent (templateVariable.percent()) takes percentage points and renders locale-aware, 12 as "12 %" in German and "12%" in English; the preview uses its example value. The document designer has no toolbar control for conditions yet; the attribute survives editing.

title: copy-locale copies the system default's files in a beforeTransaction phase and can no longer run as a nested write
detail: When a tenant copies a locale from the system default, the image and attachment files are now read and written to the tenant's storage in a beforeTransaction phase. The transaction only creates the fileRef rows, and the uploaded binaries are released when it does not commit. Before, the storage I/O held the database transaction open.
migration: Dispatch copy-locale as a top-level command, or from a perCommand handler via ctx.write. A handler that called it nested moves that call into a client or job, or becomes a perCommand handler.

title: Opening a document or mail editor with an empty body no longer marks the form as changed
detail:
Switching the editor's editable state on mount emitted an update, so DocumentTiptapEditor called onChange("

") before the user typed anything and the surrounding form counted as dirty.

title: onEditorReady receives null when the editor is destroyed
detail: DocumentTiptapEditor and PlaceholderLineEditor call onEditorReady(null) on destroy, so a held handle no longer points at a destroyed editor. The callback type is (handle: DocumentEditorHandle | null) => void. The document designer drops the handle of an unmounted field, so placeholder insertion no longer targets a destroyed editor.
migration: A custom onEditorReady callback must accept null and drop its stored handle when it receives it.

title: Document editor no longer blanks the app when late placeholders rebuild it
detail: When the system placeholders or resource previews arrived in the same render as a new value (layout editor after opening or saving), the editor rebuilt itself and the value sync then read the destroyed editor. The TypeError unmounted the whole app and left a blank page. Both sync effects now skip a destroyed editor; the replacement editor picks up the value on its next render.

title: Steps block in mail and PDF templates
detail: The document editor offers a steps block in the toolbar block menu. It stores a fixed list of stages (value=label, at most 8) and the variable that names the current stage. Mail and PDF render it as a row of bars and labels; stages up to the current one are coloured, the current label is bold. Invalid blocks are dropped by the sanitizer and render nothing. Layout regions do not offer the block.

title: A paragraph or heading that only holds an empty placeholder is left out of the rendered document
detail: compileDocumentBodyToHandlebars wraps a p or h1 to h4 whose only content is one placeholder in an if block, so an empty optional value no longer leaves a blank line in mails and PDFs. Zero numbers and money values still render. Blocks with static text, images or several placeholders are unchanged.

title: Mail layout buttons follow the branding accent colour
detail: mailLayoutAppearance takes the tenant branding accent colour. When the layout uses the branding accent line, buttons in the mail body use that colour instead of the fixed dark teal. Invalid colours fall back to the previous default.

title: A placeholder inside a button label is kept
detail: The document schema allows placeholder chips inside a button label. Before, saving or seeding a body such as a button reading "View {{pageName}}" split the button: the label stopped at the placeholder and the rest landed in a new paragraph outside the button.

title: compileDocumentBodyToHandlebars takes a height cap for resource images
detail: The new resourceImageMaxHeightPx option adds max-height and width:auto to resource images. The mail renderer caps images in a layout header at 64 px, so a square logo stays small while a wide wordmark keeps its 180 px width cap.

title: resource-upload refuses key collisions between images and attachments and linking a non-active PDF template
detail: Uploading an attachment under a key that holds an inline image, or an image under a key that holds an attachment or linked PDF, fails with template_attachment_invalid (code key_in_use) instead of silently replacing the entry. resource-link-pdf only accepts an active document-pdf template, so draft or archived templates no longer produce mails that fail at send time. When the link write fails after the file was stored, the orphaned storage object is deleted.

title: collection kinds fail at boot; validate, diff-to-system, overview, seeding, bundle import and placeholder checks follow the write rules
detail: createTemplateResolverFeature throws for a collection whose kind is mail, mail-layout or pdf-layout instead of failing on every save. The validate query ignores scope system for non-SystemAdmins. diff-to-system compares only against an active system template like reset-to-system. The overview reads rows in a stable order and reports truncated when its row limit is hit. Re-seeding notification templates reactivates an archived system row and applies a changed parentTemplateId. A bundle holds at most 50 locales. Dotted placeholders under a declared variable or list item field are reported as unknown because they never render a value. The document editor fallbacks are read-only and the placeholder line editor recolors chips when systemVariables change.

title: Resource image formats come from one list
detail: PNG, JPEG, GIF and WebP content types and extensions are defined once in the shared module and reused by the resource upload, the document body compiler and the email channel.

title: resource-upload, import-bundle and import-bundle-system upload in a beforeTransaction phase and can no longer run as nested writes
detail: The three handlers now validate and upload their files before the write transaction opens and only create the fileRef and template rows inside it, so no database connection sits idle in a transaction during storage I/O. A rolled-back transaction releases the uploaded bytes. Because they now have a pre-transaction phase, the dispatcher rejects a nested ctx.write, ctx.writeAs or handler-to-handler call of them ("has a pre-transaction phase"). The exported storeTemplateResource is replaced by prepareTemplateResourceBeforeTransaction (beforeTransaction half) and storePreparedTemplateResource (in-transaction half).
migration: Dispatch resource-upload, import-bundle and import-bundle-system as top-level commands, or from a perCommand handler via ctx.write. A handler that called them nested moves that call into a client or job, or becomes a perCommand handler. Code that called storeTemplateResource calls prepareTemplateResourceBeforeTransaction in a beforeTransaction phase and passes the result to storePreparedTemplateResource in the handler.

title: PDF collections show Page break instead of Button, and placeholder links no longer insert {{name}} text
detail: The content editor for a `document-pdf` collection now offers the PDF block set (including Page break) instead of the mail set, chosen from the collection's kind. A link to a placeholder href such as `{{invoice.url}}` without a selection now links a variable node instead of inserting the placeholder as plain text.

title: Document sanitizer rejects prototype-style placeholder hrefs
detail: `{{__proto__}}` and `{{constructor.prototype}}` are no longer accepted as link or button placeholder hrefs; only valid reference names pass.

title: DocumentRepeatRow is removed, use DocumentTableRow
detail: Removed the DocumentRepeatRow alias

title: export-bundle for a system template with resources returns a validation error outside the system tenant
detail: A TenantAdmin, or a SystemAdmin outside the system tenant, exporting a system template that links resource files now gets the `system_resources_need_system_tenant` validation error, the same code import-bundle-system uses, instead of a NotFound for the resource file.

title: send-test logs failed test mails with error class and tenant
detail: A transport that throws or reports not sent is logged with the error class/code and tenant id (no address, no provider body) and still answers `template_test_mail_failed`.

title: copy-locale ignores archived tenant sources and duplicates linked files of system sources; export-bundle refuses locales with differing format
detail: copy-locale no longer copies from an archived tenant template, and copying a system template duplicates its linked resource files into the target tenant. export-bundle rejects a bundle whose locales differ in content format or variable schema with `bundleLocalesDiffer`.

title: Template preview counts encoding overhead and reports missing attachments
detail: The mail size estimate counts base64 size plus a fixed per-part overhead, an attachment whose file reference is missing fails the resources_resolved check, and the document draft scope is derived once per request.

title: A draft no longer replaces the active template
detail: Saving a draft (upsert-tenant default, copy-locale, import-bundle with status draft) over an active template stores it beside the active version in the new column draft instead of overwriting content, meta and status; resolveTemplate, resolveLayout, preview without content and sends keep using the active version. publish and publish-system promote an open draft (the publish gate checks the draft) and record activeVersion and activeSince; the new handlers discard-draft and discard-draft-system drop it and refuse with no_draft when none is open. find-by-id and layout-source return the working version (the open draft with status draft, else the stored one) plus active { version, since }, null when nothing is served. overview keeps status and version of the served version and adds draftVersion and activeSince. A draft over a row that is not active (new, draft or archived) behaves as before. A tenant never sees system draft content: find-by-id, layout-source, overview, copy-locale and diff-to-system apply a system draft only for a SystemAdmin and hide system rows that were never served; list leaves those rows out too. Version numbers shown for an active row are the served version (activeVersion): resolveTemplate / resolveLayout results, tenant-overrides rows and the override diff no longer show the save counter that drafts raise.
migration: Run kumiko schema generate and apply the migration before deploying: it adds the nullable columns draft, active_version and active_since to read_template_resources. No rebuild needed.

title: template-resolver:query:overview accepts layoutSlug to list only the mails and PDFs using that layout
detail: The optional layoutSlug payload field keeps only documents whose layout slug matches; total counts the filtered rows. Without it the response is unchanged.

title: Layout usage follows the effective template per notification and locale
detail: Mail layout usage counts a notification only when it declares a template and resolves the effective row per notification and locale, so tenant overrides are reflected.

title: templateVariable.richText for notification variables that carry formatted HTML
detail: Notification variables are escaped, so a value holding HTML (for example a document written in a rich text editor) showed up as literal tags in the mail. A variable declared with templateVariable.richText({ required }) is run through the document sanitizer at render time and inserted as HTML; bold, italic, lists and safe links stay, script, event handlers and javascript links are not emitted as markup. If the sanitizer rejects a value, it is rendered as escaped text and a warning with the violation codes is logged. All other variable types stay escaped.

title: Overview and layout-source queries for the template designer
detail: template-resolver:query:overview lists the mail, PDF and layout templates of the caller's tenant grouped by slug and kind (effective origin, locales, status, versions, layout slug, last change and the notifications that use it) and template-resolver:query:layout-source returns the header, signature and footer regions of a mail or PDF layout plus the locale a save has to use; a SystemAdmin also receives the MJML source of the system layout. The usage lookup is the exported collectTemplateUsage.

title: contentFormat "document" with a toolbar editor for mail and PDF templates
detail: ContentEditorFormat gains "document". template-resolver registers DocumentContentEditor for it (tiptap, lazy-loaded) and stores the body as html. The toolbar offers paragraph style, bold, italic, lists, links, placeholders and the blocks image, table, button, divider, repeat and page break; the blocks prop picks them (MAIL_DOCUMENT_BLOCKS, PDF_DOCUMENT_BLOCKS). Placeholders are inserted only as variable nodes (data-variable), never as {{name}} text. ContentPreview does not substitute example values for "document" content, because substituting a button or link href would make the schema drop that node. New exports from template-resolver/web: DocumentContentEditor, DocumentEditorProps, DocumentToolbarBlock, MAIL_DOCUMENT_BLOCKS, PDF_DOCUMENT_BLOCKS.

title: Preview uses the examples of a stored or draft variable schema
detail: A template's variableSchema kept only type and required, label and example were dropped, so the preview showed [name] instead of the declared example. The schema now keeps label and example, for mail and document previews.

title: PDF meta gets orientation, printBackground and layoutHeaderFooter; paragraphs and headings get data-align
detail: The document-pdf meta accepts orientation (portrait or landscape), printBackground (default true) and layoutHeaderFooter (false prints without the layout header and footer). Paragraphs and headings carry textAlign (left, center, right, justify), serialized as data-align and kept by the sanitizer only with these four values. New exports are evaluateDocumentDraft, localeSchema, DOCUMENT_TEXT_ALIGNMENTS and DocumentTextAlign; compileDocumentBodyToHandlebars accepts alignmentAsInlineStyle.

title: document-pdf templates require contentFormat html, and html bodies are sanitized on write
detail: upsertSystem, upsertTenant, the collection-set handlers and seedSystemTemplate rebuild html bodies of kind mail-html and document-pdf through the new document schema (template-resolver/document-schema). Script elements, inline event handlers, embedded content (iframe, frame, object, embed, applet, portal), links and url attributes (svg href, xlink:href, form action, base) outside https/http/mailto/tel/{{placeholder}}, external image sources, alt text containing < or >, and invalid or prototype-chain variable names are rejected with a validation_error (or a thrown Error in seedSystemTemplate); anything the schema cannot express is dropped silently, and links keep only href (no target, rel, class or title). New exports: documentExtensions, DocumentLink and the other Document* nodes, isAllowedDocumentLinkHref, isDocumentReferenceName, isDocumentResourceKey, isDocumentPlaceholderHref, sanitizeDocumentHtml, sanitizeTemplateBody. kind document-pdf with another contentFormat is rejected with document_requires_html_format.
migration: Store document-pdf bodies as html and reference images via data-resource instead of src. mail-html with markdown or mjml is unchanged.

title: Mail templates carry file attachments (PDF, PNG, JPEG)
detail: linkedResources stays image only; file attachments of a mail template are listed in the optional TemplateResource.fileAttachments (kind file, fileRefId, fileName), sorted by key. template-resolver:write:resource-upload takes purpose "attachment" with a fileName; it checks the file by content (PDF, PNG, JPEG), keeps the original bytes, allows at most 10 per mail template and stores the entry next to the inline images. resource-remove, copy-locale and the bundle export/import carry attachments (bundle resource entries get purpose "attachment"). The preview lists attachments with kind "inline" or "file" (PreviewAttachment is now a union), send-test sends them, and the mail renderer attaches them after the inline images within the delivery attachment limit.

title: copy-locale can copy system templates (scope "system", system admins only)
detail: template-resolver:write:copy-locale takes scope "tenant" (default) or "system". With "system" a system admin copies a system template to another locale as a draft; other callers get access denied.

title: Mail preview returns displayHtml for the editor
detail: The preview of a mail template carries displayHtml, the body with cid images replaced by data URIs (png, jpeg, gif, webp, 5 MiB budget in total) so an editor can show it without cid support. The sent mail is unchanged.

title: Document editor gets variable labels, a handle, resource previews, canvas chrome, underline and PlaceholderLineEditor
detail: DocumentContentEditor accepts variableLabels, systemVariables, resourcePreviews, chrome ("default" or "canvas") and onEditorReady (handle with insertPlaceholder, insertResource, focus). The new PlaceholderLineEditor edits plain text with {{name}} placeholders as chips on one line. Underline (u) is part of the document schema and survives the sanitizer.

title: Mail templates link a PDF rendered from a document template (resource-link-pdf)
detail: New write template-resolver:write:resource-link-pdf takes templateId, key, templateSlug and fileName and stores a linkedResources entry { kind "rendered-pdf", templateSlug, fileName } in a mail template; nothing is uploaded. fileName is a one-line pattern that may use the mail's {{placeholders}} and must end with .pdf (no / \ " ; or ..). The document-pdf template must exist for the tenant or the system, otherwise the write fails with template_attachment_pdf_template_missing; an invalid pattern or slug fails with template_attachment_invalid. Uploaded files and linked PDFs share the limit of 10 attachments per template. resource-remove, copy-locale and the bundle export/import carry the entry (the bundle gets an optional pdfAttachments map of key to { templateSlug, fileName }; import does not check that the document template exists). TemplateResource gains pdfAttachmentLinks, LinkedResourceEntry gains the TemplatePdfAttachmentLink variant.

title: Preview and test mail use the images and attachments of the edited row, also while it is a draft
detail: When preview or send-test get content and the caller has a row for (slug, kind, locale), that row supplies linkedResources whatever its status (also when it has none, so nothing is borrowed from the system template), so a tenant whose customization is saved as a draft sees its logo and attachments. MailDraft has an optional linkedResources; without it the stored active template's resources are used as before. PreviewAttachment gains the variant { kind "rendered-pdf", name, templateSlug } without sizeBytes, because the PDF is not rendered in the preview; size_under_cap does not count it.

title: Preview query and send-test write for mail and PDF templates
detail: template-resolver:query:preview renders a draft, or the stored template when no content is given, with sample values from the declared variable examples (list variables get two rows). The draft passes the same write gates as a save and a mail goes through the real mail renderer, so subject, html, plain text and inline images match a real send. The response carries checks (images resolved, plain text present, size under 10 MiB, required placeholders used); a PDF template returns its sanitized body and the layout regions. template-resolver:write:send-test mails the rendered mail to the calling user's own address only, subject prefixed with [TEST], limited to 10 per user and hour. It needs delivery, channel-email and renderer-mail-html.

title: DocumentEditorProps toolbar option for an icon-only toolbar
detail: DocumentEditorProps gains toolbar ("full" or "compact", default "full"). Compact renders the placeholder and block buttons icon-only with a tooltip and a narrower paragraph select, for narrow columns such as the layout editor regions. The formatting buttons now carry a tooltip with their label in every mode.

title: kind mail-html is replaced by mail, mail-layout and pdf-layout; templates carry meta
detail: The kind mail-html is removed; the new non-render kind snippet holds collection content (reply snippets, signatures; any contentFormat, html is sanitized like a mail body). Mail bodies are kind mail (contentFormat html only, rebuilt through the document schema, meta.subject required), mail frames are kind mail-layout (contentFormat mjml), and pdf-layout (html) is new. The table gains a nullable meta column (JSON per kind, validated by parseTemplateMeta: mail takes subject, previewText, layoutSlug, category, sender; layouts take none; other kinds take no meta) and the template-resource entity moves to eventVersion 2 with an upcaster that reads stored mail-html events as mail. upsertSystem, upsertTenant (active), publish and seedSystemTemplate reject unknown placeholders and, for the same writes, bodies that miss a required variable of the notification with the same qualified name; a tenant draft may be incomplete and returns validation. Slugs must be kebab segments joined by a colon. seedSystemTemplate now validates the slug (templateSlugSchema) and the per-kind meta for every kind. A content collection of kind mail, mail-layout or pdf-layout is refused on collection-set (field issue on kind, templateResolver.errors.collection.kindNotAllowed), because such a tenant row would shadow the system template without the meta and placeholder gates. TemplateResource gains meta. New exports: parseTemplateMeta, isMailTemplateMeta, templateSlugSchema, validateTemplatePlaceholders, resolveTemplateVariables, compileDocumentBodyToHandlebars, MAIL_CATEGORIES and their types; seedNotificationTemplates and hasNotificationTemplates on template-resolver/seeding, which applyBootSeeds now calls. RENDER_KINDS contains mail instead of mail-html.
migration: Rename kind mail-html to mail in app code, collections and seeds; mail bodies must be contentFormat html (markdown or mjml mail bodies are rejected) and carry meta.subject, mail layouts use kind mail-layout with contentFormat mjml and slug default. Slugs of every kind must now be kebab segments joined by a colon (upsert handlers and seedSystemTemplate reject dotted, underscored or camelCase slugs). Collections that used kind mail-html move to the new kind snippet (stored mail-html rows are upcast to mail, which collections refuse, so re-create those entries under snippet); collection-set refuses mail, mail-layout and pdf-layout collections. seedSystemTemplate callers must pass a kebab slug and valid meta for every kind, not only mail. Generate and apply the migration that adds the nullable meta column to read_template_resources; it ships a rebuild marker for read_template_resources so existing mail-html rows are read as mail after the rebuild.

title: resolveLayout finds a layout in any locale
detail: TemplateResolverApi gains resolveLayout({ tenantId, slug, kind, locale }) for mail-layout and pdf-layout. It looks at the tenant first (requested locale, then the fallback locale, then any active locale) and then at the system layouts the same way, ignoring draft and archived rows. A layout saved by the layout editor under one locale is therefore found for every locale. The template preview uses it for the PDF layout.

title: PDF template meta, render provenance, system template lifecycle and override queries
detail: kind document-pdf takes a strict meta (layoutSlug, pageFormat A4/Letter, margins in mm, fileName without / \ " ; or .., metadata title/author); new exports PDF_PAGE_FORMATS, PdfPageFormat, PdfTemplateMeta, readPdfTemplateMeta, DEFAULT_MAIL_LAYOUT_SLUG. RenderResponse (renderer-foundation) gains optional template and layout refs ({ templateId, templateVersion, scope }, new types RenderedTemplateRef and RenderProvenance); renderer-mail-html fills them. New handlers template-resolver:write:publish-system and archive-system (SystemAdmin), reset-to-system (TenantAdmin, SystemAdmin), queries usage, tenant-overrides (SystemAdmin, counts only) and diff-to-system. publish and archive answer not_found for rows outside the caller's tenant instead of a version_conflict; find-by-id also returns meta.

title: linkedResources is no longer a payload field of upsertSystem/upsertTenant; resourceUpload and resourceRemove manage it
detail: Two steps - upload the image with POST /api/files (multipart, no entityType), then call template-resolver:write:resource-upload with { sourceFileRefId, templateId?, key? }. The handler re-encodes the caller's own unclaimed upload into a new file ref (width at most 1200 px) and links it into the template; resource-remove unlinks a key. upsertSystem and upsertTenant no longer accept linkedResources and leave the stored value untouched on update. The size cap is the system config key resource-max-bytes (default 2 MiB); a cap above the files route's maxUploadSize has no effect because the upload is rejected first. The source upload stays as an unclaimed file.
migration: Whoever sent linkedResources with upsertSystem or upsertTenant now uploads the image via POST /api/files (multipart, no entityType) and links it with template-resolver:write:resource-upload { sourceFileRefId, templateId, key }. Server-side seeding (seedSystemTemplate linkedResources) stays.

title: Bundle import re-encodes its images like resource-upload; re-seeding keeps uploaded system resources
detail: importBundle and importBundleSystem store each bundle resource through the same normalization as resource-upload (decoded format decides the content type, SVG and non-images are rejected, width at most 1200 px, resource-max-bytes applies), so an exported bundle carries the re-encoded bytes. seedSystemTemplate without linkedResources no longer resets the links of an existing row, so images a system admin uploaded survive the next boot. storeTemplateResource from the template-resolver barrel is the normalizing store; the raw byte variant is gone.

title: Tenant mail-layouts are structured html, pdf-layout and document-pdf are placeholder-validated
detail: A new validate query dry-runs the write pipeline (used, unknown and missing placeholders, canSave, canPublish). document-pdf, pdf-layout and mail-layout now go through the same placeholder gate as mail; document-pdf and pdf-layout know the system placeholders page and pages. A tenant mail-layout is html with a data-content slot plus header, signature and footer regions that renderer-mail-html wraps in a fixed MJML frame; raw mjml (with {{{content}}} exactly once) is system-only. New handlers export-bundle, import-bundle, import-bundle-system and copy-locale move a template with its resource files between tenants and locales. r.notification accepts a record mapping from an entity row to the declared variables, validated at boot. publish and archive no longer touch system rows through a tenant-scoped SystemAdmin.
migration: Tenant mail-layout rows stored as mjml are ignored by the renderer, which falls back to the system layout; re-create them as html with a data-content slot. upsert-system answers with an extra validation field. seedSystemTemplate errors now read `<label> rejected: <code> (<detail>); ...`. Layout bodies without the content slot are rejected on write. `set` now runs the same gate for mail, document-pdf, pdf-layout and mail-layout rows and rejects unsanitized markup or publish issues, since saving publishes; the mail renderer also re-sanitizes stored tenant html layouts and falls back to the system layout when they fail. upsert-system and upsert-tenant no longer accept linkedResources (resources go through the resource upload; bundle import and copy-locale attach them). Unknown data-resource keys are a validate warning (resource_not_uploaded), not a write error.

title: template-resolver list filters by every template kind including text-block and ai-prompt
TemplateResource and text-block/collection query outputs expose modifiedAt instead of updatedAt
detail:
Review round 2 fixes across the feature AST, codemods, the template-resolver and the renderer router.
- feature-ast: handler lookup falls back to the header when the body carries no match, a `zod` namespace import (`import * as z`) is recognised, and patch edits no longer overlap.
- Codemods: the PII heuristic matches segment-aligned names, the open-to-all codemod sets its exit code, and `failUnprocessable` calls are migrated.
- template-resolver: the row types and the public output now use the real base columns. `by-slug`, `by-tenant`, `list`, `find-by-id` and the `TemplateResource` API return `modifiedAt` (null until the first edit) instead of `updatedAt`, which was always undefined at runtime. The user-content export reads `modifiedAt` too.
- renderer: `formatPath` and `parsePath` encode and decode every path segment, so an entity id like `foo/bar` or `ä b` survives a round trip. A malformed percent-escape in the URL resolves to no route.
migration: Rename reads of `updatedAt` to `modifiedAt` on TemplateResource, the by-slug, by-tenant, list, find-by-id and collection queries, and the template-resolver web BlockSummary. The old field was never populated at runtime; the new one is an ISO timestamp, or null for a row that was never edited.

title: ContentEditorProps gains a required id (fw#2001).
detail: TextBlockEditor's Field wrapping a registered "rich"/"plain" editor pointed its htmlFor at the fixed CONTENT_EDITOR_ELEMENT_ID, which only the never-mounted textarea fallback actually used — the label was disconnected from the real input as soon as a collection declared contentFormat: "rich" or "plain". TextBlockEditor now generates a per-instance id via useId() and passes it to both the Field and the ContentEditor, so the label stays correctly associated and two editors mounted on the same page no longer collide on a shared DOM id.
migration: A custom-registered content editor component now needs to accept and use this id prop, rendering it onto its own focusable root element. Consumers that don't touch the DOM id directly are unaffected. CONTENT_EDITOR_ELEMENT_ID stays exported as a default value for callers that don't need their own generated id.
